newsitem.title: USA: Nazis, collaborators may be on Swiss bank list.
newsitem.headline: Nazis, collaborators may be on Swiss bank list.

text.p: The just-published list of almost 2,000 dormant Holocaust-era Swiss bank accounts may include the names of key Nazi figures and a man who helped the Third Reich loot the art treasures of Europe, Jewish groups said on Wednesday.

While Holocaust survivors and their heirs around the world scoured the list, the Los Angeles-based Simon Wiesenthal Centre and New York's World Jewish Congress said several names on the list were troubling.

The Wiesenthal Centre sent a letter to the Swiss Bankers Association saying that six names on the list might be members of Hitler's Nazi elite, including an aide to mass murderer Adolf Eichmann and the wife of the head of Nazi intelligence.

Meanwhile, the World Jewish Congress said it was concerned that the list contained the name of a Dr. Hans Wendland because that was also the name of one of the most notorious dealers in looted Nazi art during the war.
A WJC spokesman said Wendland fenced stolen Old Master and impressionist paintings from Jewish collections now worth hundreds of millions of dollars.

Jewish leaders who have led an international battle for two years for the names of lost account holders praised Swiss banks for breaking their strict code of secrecy and publishing a list of 1,840 dormant accounts worth about $42 million without interest.

Swiss Bankers Association chairman Georg Krayer said just a glance at the list published in newspapers in 27 countries and on the Internet (www.dormantaccounts.ch) showed names that could have been tracked down by banks if they had tried.

"I was somewhat ashamed ... I have not found a figleaf big enough to cover up the negligence of my banking colleagues in the period after the Second World War," Krayer told a joint news conference with Jewish leaders.
WJC Vice President Kalman Sultanik said the reaction to the list was electrifying but added, "We always assumed that on the list would be the names of Nazis and their collaborators.

"Documents in the U.S. National Archives clearly show that looted assets and not just Holocaust victims' accounts were placed in Swiss financial institutions to take advantage of Swiss bank secrecy laws."
The Wiesenthal Centre said it was concerned about six names on the list: Willy Bauer, Elisabeth Eder, Hermann Esser, Hermann Schmitz, Heinrich Hoffman and Karl Jager.

Bauer was an alias used by Anton Burger, an Eichmann aide and deputy commandant of the Theresienstadt concentration camp; Eder was the wife of Ernst Kaltenbrunner, the head of the SD, the Nazis' intelligence arm; Esser was vice president of the Reichstag; Hoffmann was a Hitler confidant and Jager the head of Nazi inteilligence in Lithuania.

Rabbi Marvin Hier, the dean of the Wiesenthal Centre, said his group had supplied the German Finance Ministry with a list of 342 members of the Nazi elite so that their financial records could be tracked.
He said he hoped the Swiss Bankers Association would provide the necessary details to determine if the six names his organisation was concerned about were indeed members of the Nazi elite.
